# Security Verification -- STS Work Order App

**Date:** 2026-06-04
**Codebase:** github.com/vioverse-io/prepress-server (SQL Server version)
**Generated by:** Claude (Anthropic), requested by David Marra

---

## Summary

The app is clean. It does not send data anywhere, does not contain hidden code, and does not access anything on the server beyond its own database. Everything is readable and verifiable.

---

## What the app does

- Users fill out print job checklists in a browser
- Data saves to your SQL Server (two tables: `jobs` and `components`)
- The Node.js server sits between the browser and SQL Server -- it reads and writes to those two tables and nothing else
- No emails sent, no cloud services contacted, no external APIs called

## What the app does NOT do

- Does not make any calls to the internet
- Does not access the filesystem (no reading/writing files on the server)
- Does not run system commands
- Does not set cookies or track users
- Does not contain any hidden or scrambled code

---

## SQL injection protection

User input never goes directly into SQL queries. Every value is passed as a named parameter (`@id`, `@jobNumber`, etc.), which is the standard safe practice. You can verify this yourself -- see below.

## Server dependencies

The server uses only 3 packages (plus 1 optional):

| Package | What it does |
|---------|-------------|
| express | Web server (industry standard, ~35 million weekly downloads) |
| mssql | Connects to SQL Server |
| dotenv | Reads the .env config file |
| msnodesqlv8 (optional) | Enables Windows Authentication |

No unusual or obscure packages.

## Database access

The app supports two authentication modes (set via `SQL_AUTH` in `.env`). **SQL auth** uses a SQL Server username and password stored in `.env`. **Windows auth** uses the Windows account running the Node process (no SQL credentials stored). Either way, the account only needs `db_datareader` and `db_datawriter` roles (cannot alter the database structure or access other databases).

---

## How to verify this yourself

You do not need to take anyone's word for it. The server code is short enough to read in full.

**Step 1: Read the entire server (457 lines)**

Open `server-sql/server.js` in any text editor. This is the complete backend. Every API endpoint is visible. Look for anything that seems out of place -- you won't find it.

**Step 2: Read the database connection (56 lines)**

Open `server-sql/db.js`. This is the complete database layer. It connects to SQL Server using your .env settings and nothing else.

**Step 3: Check that SQL queries are safe**

In `server.js`, search for `.query(`. Every query you find will have `.input()` calls above it -- those are the parameterized values. If you see user data going directly into a query string without `.input()`, that would be a problem. There are none.

**Step 4: Check that the server doesn't access the filesystem or run commands**

Search `server.js` and `db.js` for these words: `child_process`, `exec`, `spawn`, `fs`, `readFile`, `writeFile`. None of them appear.

**Step 5: Check the SQL scripts**

Open `server-sql/sql/create-database.sql` and `create-tables.sql`. They create one database and two tables. No stored procedures, no triggers, no xp_cmdshell, no linked servers.

---

**Total files to review: 4 files, under 600 lines combined.** That covers 100% of the server-side code.
